Scope and authority: reviewed only quality point 47. Opened the actual frozen rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx with openpyxl: Quality Checks worksheet row 48 explicitly requires the shared pinned agent/model, CLIs/browser and fixed-clock graded rules, while saying temperature and prompt-version markers are not required and public verifier networking/missing allowlists are NOT defects. Also inspected Internal Quality Checks row 48; its older temperature-0/no-unpinned-network annotation does not override the shipped row. Inspected Deterministic Checks rows 2, 7, 10, 11 and 17, the frozen SKILL.md Delivery profile, quality-checks.md:187-189, staged-task-contract.md sections task.toml, tests/tools and Cross-file agreements, deterministic-checks.md canonical/Docker/network recipes, and current qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md. All 50 frozen task files independently matched the task hashes in qc/runs/coldwater-2026-09-30-hardening/manifest.json, whose input_sha256 matches this assignment. Paths below beginning task/ and rules/ are relative to .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-hardening/.

Pins and canonical code: task/task.toml:30-35 sets REWARDKIT_JUDGE = "claude-code", REWARDKIT_MODEL = "z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx", the OpenRouter URL and the canonical credential-variable wiring. Parsed equality against the frozen template verifier.env was true. Parsed all five judge.toml files: each uses the same claude-code fallback and Playwright command with --executable-path=/usr/local/bin/chromium; none overrides the model, temperature, reasoning effort or judge weight. task/tests/Dockerfile:16-21 pins @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.281, @openai/codex@0.151.0, @playwright/mcp@0.0.79, express@5.1.0 and better-sqlite3@12.4.1; line 31 pins harbor-rewardkit==0.1.7. Lines 33-38 install Chromium through the Playwright distribution under that installed MCP package and link its binary to the path all five judges use. This is the shipped template's browser pinning mechanism; the source does not select an OS browser or a latest channel. Independently compared bytes against rules/projects/webdev-task-template: tests/Dockerfile, tests/test.sh, tests/scoring.toml and both tests/tools files are identical. SHA256 values are Dockerfile 72998ab8ef0e4225e63b88fccdb754943c54022e25da355035efe7f759a55fdd, test.sh bd68259276ca4b034654efc8a1723a4e702ed62dbe590af6201565f43eabe5aa, score.py 13de2b3885967e22aa13ded3bf33c354e3e741e85be871612c04e996eef5c04e, restart_mcp.py 03c1426f00e451f4d86b7547761715328c63cdf299f5f812f46c9fa3b44979b5, scoring.toml 95f70d6e06aae5e765b2309d88c444aa36d4cd82763ea2212781b6a99311bbba. Read both shared tool implementations and test.sh. The scorer computes solely from the fixed scoring policy and returned finite dimension values; the restart helper's date at test.sh:178 is diagnostic logging, not grading input. The inherited version-tag base images and unpinned apt packages are not a task-specific divergence; the workbook explicitly calls unpinned apt a Note. This does not assert bit-identical future container rebuilds or provider-level model immutability.

Time rules: no calendar-date-dependent expected figure, expiry, seed date or business clock was found in the seed, all five judge configurations/prompts, app context, harness or tools. A fixed calendar clock is therefore inapplicable to this product. environment/instructions/behaviour.md:9 defines an elapsed five-second run budget including callbacks, and :21 defines elapsed typing-pause behavior. tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:15 measures from the actual Run/interaction and permits scheduling overhead; :334-338 measures the actual debounce instead of imposing a hard-coded debounce value, and rejects a missed setup window as proof of product failure. :399-408 batches callback/deadline observation and uses a positive 200+200 ms callback control against the 3000+3000 ms forbidden completion, rather than separate LLM timestamps. Date.now() at :36 generates a probe nonce, not an expected time or graded figure; changing the run date changes the two generated URLs and their expected token together. Freezing the real execution clock would undermine the elapsed-time behavior being measured.

Network fixtures: task/task.toml:22,38 deliberately sets both phases public. instruction.md:9, environment/instructions/security.md:9, tests/app_context.md:20 and tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:13 all permit app fonts/scripts/CDNs while imposing the separately requested boundary on authored snippets. The functional prompt's supplied recipe at :27-95 routes exactly two fresh URLs under cw-qc-network.invalid and fulfills fixed text/SVG responses locally (:43-49); :63 requires the expected text, width 2 and exactly two successful control deliveries. The negative run compares deliveries against this observed baseline. :204 explicitly says the control contacts no internet and failed setup is unavailable evidence, not a product failure or pass. These are deterministic local test responses, not remotely fetched reference data.

Raw observations: independently read qc/runs/coldwater-2026-09-30-hardening/golden/run-golden-20260930-070504/RESULTS.json and its executed drivers. The raw runtime identifies Chromium 152.0.7977.8, MCP 0.0.79, paid_provider=false, network=none and direct pinned Playwright. The functional prompt and judge file hashes in that record independently match the current frozen files (6405c6c52916b9480837a98b228a26e5fa0465241a3003d6da71b5f2bab907d1 and 8e309112e55b495ff94bcc420483dc844b865bdf93cd3008522829914c2f3a2d). Independently hash-checked boundary_flow.cjs, runtime_flow.cjs, current_flow.cjs, workflow_core.cjs and run_workflow.cjs against the raw record's driver_sha256 entries. facts.S07.snippet_network_boundary.evidence records the expected text nonce, image width 2, baseline=2, both visible refusals, both loaded=false, final_deliveries=2, fulfilled_locally=true and recovery. boundary_flow.cjs:24-35 confirms these came from local route fulfillment and explicit successful transport controls. facts.S09.literal_loop_deadline records 5001.299, 5006.031 and 5002.286 ms for the three loop probes. facts.S17.autorun_debounce records a 546.428 ms initial automatic run and 550.046 ms final delay with no intermediate execution. facts.S36.callback_shared_run_deadline records nested-control-done, late-callback-entered, a five-second time-limit reason and no forbidden-nested-completion; current_flow.cjs:41-47 and run_workflow.cjs:34 show the actual dispatched 200/3000 ms nested-timer protocol and ten-second observation. These are scripted product observations, not full configured LLM judge timing or an Oracle score.

Adversarial reasoning: a conforming app may load an external editor/font and use a separate local preview host; the source explicitly permits both, and the S07 route handler affects only its exact two probe URLs, so it does not reject that alternative. A run on another calendar date changes only a self-consistent nonce; no expected calendar output changes. A broken app that allows the authored fetch/Image traffic would cause extra locally intercepted deliveries (and potentially EXTERNAL_*_LOADED); it cannot gain a pass merely because public DNS is unavailable. A dead runner cannot satisfy the required ordinary execution and transport controls. These are source-level counterexample attempts, not newly executed alternative-app runs; no credible false-pass/false-fail witness specific to point 47 was established.

Limits: did not launch Docker, install packages, contact a provider or run the full configured judge. Exact provider repeatability, future clean-build identity, full judge completion time, hosted Oracle and target-model scores remain unmeasured. The runtime verdict is PARTIAL because the raw scripted browser observations support local fixtures and elapsed behavior but do not exercise the complete paid judge. This point's Pass is limited to the specified source pinning and fixture-determinism contract; it is not overall QC clearance.
